summary: Emanuel Sarkisyanz (1923–2015) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tehran and completed his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago, later serving as Head at Heidelberg University from 1967.

Emanuela Garatti is a Tibetologist who earned her doctorate at the École Pratique des Hautes Études. She held an affiliated post at the University of Munich (attested 2018) and served as ATER at the EPHE in 2022.

Embar Krishnamacharya was an Indologist. He served as a pandit at the Oriental Manuscripts Library and held positions with the Gaekwad's Oriental Series (attested 1926), Sanskrit Pathashala, Vadtal (attested 1937), and Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya, Vadodara (attested 1939).

Emi Matsushita (b. 1970) specializes in history and archaeology. She studied at Nanzan University, the University of East Anglia, and Ohio State University under MA supervisor John C. Huntington, later serving there as a graduate assistant (1999–2001).

Emil Abegg (1885–1962) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at the Universities of Zurich (Ph.D.) and Leipzig under Adolf Kaegi, Ernst Windisch, Eduard Sievers, and August Conrady, later becoming Professor at Zurich (1928–1955).

Emil Ernst Strohal (1874–1902) was an Indologist. He studied at the Universities of Graz, Vienna under Georg Bühler, Leipzig, and Göttingen, where he completed his Ph.D. under Ernst Windisch, Franz Kielhorn, and Johann Kirste.

Emil Franke (1880–1939) worked in Indology. He studied at Charles University (Faculty of Arts and Faculty of Law) under Josef Zubatý, as well as the Universities of Vienna and Berlin, and later held a post at the National Library.

Emil Rödiger (1801–1874) worked in linguistics and religious studies. After earning his Dr. phil. and Lic. theol. at the University of Halle, he held professorships at Halle (1830–1860) and Humboldt University of Berlin (from 1860).

Emil Schlagintweit (1835–1904) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He was tutored by Franz Joseph Lauth and studied law at Humboldt University of Berlin before serving as a Bavarian Regierungsrat in the Government of Bavaria.

Emil Schmidt (1837–1906) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Jena, Leipzig, Bonn, and Berlin (M.D. ~1861). At the University of Leipzig, he served as Privatdozent (1885), Associate Professor of Ethnology (1890), and Honorarprofessor (1896).

Emil Sieg (1866–1951) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Berlin (Ph.D. 1891), Tübingen, and Munich under Weber, Geldner, Schmidt, Kuhn, and Kielhorn. In 1920, he held a chair at the University of Göttingen.

Emile Joseph Dillon (1854–1933) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at several institutions, earning doctorates from KU Leuven and the University of Kharkiv, where he was appointed Professor in 1884.

Emilio Bartoli (b. 1861) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Michele Kerbaker. He taught Latin and Greek at Liceo Classico Statale Vittorio Emanuele II and lectured on comparative grammar and Sanskrit at the University of Naples (1923–1925).

Emilio Lovarini (1866–1955) worked in Indology and literature. After completing his dissertation at the University of Padua (~1889), he served as Docent of Italian Literature at the University of Bologna (1900) and taught at Liceo Luigi Galvani (1904–1929).

Emilio Teza (1831–1912) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Padua and Vienna under Anton Boller, and served as Ordinarius at the Universities of Bologna (1860–1866), Pisa (1866–1889), and Padua (1889–1912).

Emily T. Yeh (b. 1971) is a Tibetologist. She studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and the University of California, Berkeley, and joined the faculty at the University of Colorado Boulder around 2003.

Emma Georgina Rothschild (b. 1948) is a historian. She studied at Somerville College and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, later holding professorial posts at the University of Cambridge (~1988) and Harvard University (~2008).

Emma J. Flatt (b. 1976) specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. She was an Assistant Professor at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (2012–2021) and became an Associate Professor at Nanyang Technological University in 2023.

Emma Salter specializes in religious studies and Indology, having studied at the University of Glamorgan, Cardiff University, and the University of Huddersfield. She taught at the Open University and Greenhead College, becoming Principal Examiner for World Religions at IB in 2019.

Emmanuel Forchhammer (1851–1890) worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leipzig under Brockhaus, von der Gabelentz, and Fleischer, later serving as chair of Pāli at Rangoon (1878) and Archaeological Inspector for British Burma (1882).
